newsitem.title: CHILE: Chile shares end firm, rally seen continuing.
newsitem.headline: Chile shares end firm, rally seen continuing.

text.p: Bucking Wall Street, Chilean shares stretched their winning run to close higher on strong demand from institutional investors with the rally seen resuming at Wednesday's opening, said traders.
"The market rose amid strong turnover, which is a good, important sign," said one dealer.
The 40-share IPSA index ended unofficially up 1.1 percent at 103.07 points. The general IGPA index firmed 0.73 percent at 5,603.28 points.

Volume swelled to 14.5 billion pesos from 8.8 billion pesos on Monday. Traders said the rise in turnover reflected a wave of buy orders from major players, including foreign investment funds and local pension funds.
These investors, who have stayed on the sidelines for months, are betting the Central Bank may cut interest rates as soon as early December, said traders.
Bank president Carlos Massad previously said the bank will only ease its restrictive monetary policy in the first quarter of next year when Chile's robust economic growth is firmly under control.
Gains included forestry firm Masisa, which rose nearly six percent on local demand, said dealers.
But they added the stock's tight liquidity meant the rise was artificially high.
Masisa, Chile's largest wood board producer, ended up 5.91 percent at 215 pesos.
Other winners included Banco de A.Edwards, up 4.4 percent at 47.5 pesos and steel-maker Cap, which firmed 2.24 percent at 1,370 pesos.
Losers included Banco de Santiago B stock, down 3.49 percent at 12.45 pesos, power distributor Chilectra, down 0.22 percent at 2,290 pesos and bottler Andina, which shed 0.21 percent at 2,370 pesos.
